text:
maria.nguyen: heads up — nightly eval run r-20260320-03 jumped failure rate from ~2% to ~18% on the 'creative-prompts' promptset. failures look like sampling/wording drift, not hallucinations. anyone else seeing stochastic noise spikes?

- eval-bot: nightly-run r-20260320-03 summary: failures +16% vs baseline; median top_p observed 0.92 (expected ~0.85), median temp computed 0.70. affected variants: model-v2-q4f16 primarily. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/r-20260320-03/ (logs + samples)

maria.nguyen: quick manual glance — fp16 hosted copies look normal, quantized (q4f16) outputs are different even with same seed. suspect sampling stack change after runtime image bump on 2026-03-19.

ahmed.khan: is this confined to q4f16? could also be a kernel reorder in quant path. any config diffs?

taylor.chen: I noticed the inference runtime image moved from inference-runtime:2026-03-15 -> inference-runtime:2026-03-19 (PR #412). PR touched sampler fallback and RNG initialization. running a tiny repro now. :mag:

```bash
# repro script I used
python repro_sampling.py \
  --model redwood/model-v2-q4f16 \
  --prompt "Write a haiku about routers" \
  --top_p 0.8 --temp 0.7 --seed 42 \
  --num_samples 3 > samples.out
```

# outputs differ from nightly-run r-20260315 for same seed
# diff highlights token sequence divergence early (after first 6 tokens)
```diff
- routers hum softly in the night,
+ routers hum gently through wires,
```

ahmed.khan: that matches what I see in a quick loop. fp16 path reproduces old output with same seed. q4 path diverges.

maria.nguyen: could this be RNG backend change? I remember we switched the default sampler RNG from python random -> numpy.random -> torch.Generator in different components historically. taylor, does PR #412 change the RNG source?

taylor.chen: yes, PR #412 added an opt-in to use torch.Generator for batching perf; default was supposed to stay the same, but there was a small refactor that accidentally made use_torch_rng=true by default for quantized runtime. here's the minimal config diff from the canary image: 

```diff
- sampler:
-   backend: legacy
-   use_torch_rng: false
+ sampler:
+   backend: legacy
+   use_torch_rng: true  # accidental default change
```

ahmed.khan: that would explain deterministic seed mapping differences — torch.Generator hashing + device stream ordering can shift token sampling when continuous batching is on. seeds aren't 1:1 across backends.

maria.nguyen: plan: 1) roll canary back to inference-runtime:2026-03-15 on 2 nodes, run short nightly subset; 2) add compatibility layer that maps legacy seed -> torch seed (hash + salt) for q4 path; 3) add test in evals to assert identical samples across backend toggle for a set of canonical prompts. sounds good?

zach-oncall-bot: rollback scheduled: inference-runtime canary -> inference-runtime:2026-03-15 on service/redwood-infer-canary-2 at 2026-03-20T03:40Z (initiated).

taylor.chen: quick local test — forcing use_torch_rng=false on the new image reproduces the older outputs exactly for the repro prompt. so yes, the backend flip is the cause. pushing a tiny config hotfix and re-running subset now.

ahmed.khan: I'll prototype a legacy->torch seed mapper this morning. simple approach: sha256(seed || "legacy-seed") % 2**32 into torch.Generator; run it against nightly corpus to measure deviation.

maria.nguyen: great. also let's add an eval that runs on q4f16 variants with seed=42 across both backends and fails CI if outputs drift beyond token-level edit distance threshold. we need that to prevent regressions from runtime image churn.

eval-bot: quick re-run r-20260320-03-subset started (subset of 200 prompts). will post artifact link when done.

maria.nguyen: thanks — keep thread updates short. if the rollback fixes the subset, we'll treat this as a regression introduced by PR #412 and revert default until a compatibility shim exists. :thumbsup:

taylor.chen: update: subset run shows failure rate back down to ~3% on the two rolled-back canary nodes. will open rollback PR and include config guard.

ahmed.khan: noted. I'll open a draft PR with seed-mapper and some perf numbers. linking once ready.

maria.nguyen: fine triage — assigning follow-up tickets: INF-2381 (rollback + guard), INF-2382 (seed compat shim + tests), EVAL-512 (e2e eval to prevent future sampler backend flips).

maria.nguyen: thanks everyone. keep small updates here; escalate if rollback doesn't hold or subset still flakes.
